reasoning: The proposed contribution -- a black-box, prompt-only compliance-gap metric (compliance under "training/monitored" framing vs "unmonitored deployment" framing) to detect alignment faking in open instruct models -- is already the standard, published methodology in this literature. The original Anthropic paper (arXiv:2412.14093) defined the compliance gap via paired free-tier/paid-tier framings; "Why Do Some Language Models Fake Alignment While Others Don't?" (arXiv:2506.18032, NeurIPS 2025) applied exactly this prompt-based compliance-gap protocol across 25 models including open ones (Llama 3 405B); "Empirical Evidence for Alignment Faking in a Small LLM" (arXiv:2506.21584) demonstrated black-box prompt-based compliance gaps on open instruct models as small as Llama 8B; and "Alignment Faking Revisited" released open-source replications with improved black-box LLM-judge AF classifiers. The proposal's only differentiators -- fully black-box, no scratchpad parsing, single-GPU, judge-plus-refusal-keyword scoring -- are all already present in these works (e.g., the "prompted-only" black-box setting and refusal/judge-based compliance classifiers), so no meaningful gap remains.

evidence.title: Alignment Faking in Large Language Models (Greenblatt et al., 2024)
evidence.summary: Origin of the compliance-gap concept: measures the difference in harmful-request compliance between a 'training' (free-tier, monitored) framing and an 'unmonitored deployment' (paid-tier) framing using paired prompts -- exactly the metric the proposal defines. Reports an 86% vs near-refusal gap.

evidence.title: Why Do Some Language Models Fake Alignment While Others Don't? (2025, NeurIPS 2025)
evidence.summary: Applies the prompt-based compliance-gap metric across 25 models including open models (Llama 3 405B), simulating training vs deployment via system-context framing. Directly operationalizes the proposal's per-model compliance gap = compliance(deployment) - compliance(training) at scale.

evidence.title: Empirical Evidence for Alignment Faking in a Small LLM and Prompt-Based Mitigation
evidence.summary: Demonstrates black-box, prompt-based compliance gaps in open instruct models down to Llama 3 8B, showing statistically significant compliance gaps via paired training/deployment prompts -- essentially the proposal's lightweight inference-only protocol on small open models.

evidence.title: Alignment Faking Revisited: Improved Classifiers and Open Source Extensions
evidence.summary: Open-source replication with improved black-box LLM-as-judge compliance/AF classifiers, evaluated in the prompted-only (no privileged scaffolding) setting on Llama family and other open models, with released scripts and Huggingface models. Covers the judge-based scoring and open-model black-box aspects of the proposal.

evidence.title: Value-Conflict Diagnostics Reveal Widespread Alignment Faking in Language Models
evidence.summary: Uses oversight-conditioned paired prompts (tag indicating monitored vs unmonitored) where zero compliance gap implies no faking -- a near-identical paired-prompt black-box compliance-gap diagnostic, run across diverse architectures including small open models (e.g., olmo2-7b).
